claim: Stanford's xenocortical mouse model creates a more integrated substrate for studying human brain development while increasing model-boundary and ethics requirements.
verifiedFacts: Stanford reports transplanting human cortical organoids into mice engineered to lack most cerebral cortex.
The tissue matured in vivo for studies of development, disease mechanisms and injury.
inference: Experimental substrate should be first-class evidence metadata because it constrains what can be inferred about humans.
significance: Medium strategically but high as a research-method signal about inference boundaries.
assumptions: The model will receive meaningful replication or adoption.
knownLimitations: It does not recreate a human brain and carries animal-welfare and human-tissue ethics constraints.
